summary.name: LMMS
summary.one_liner: LMMS is a free, open source, multiplatform digital audio workstation for making beats, composing music, and mixing sounds.
use_cases: Making beats and melodies on a computer
Playing instruments with a MIDI or typing keyboard
Mixing and automating track levels and effects
Creating retro chiptune-style sounds with emulated synths
Importing MIDI or Hydrogen projects to continue work
summary.what_it_does: LMMS lets users sequence, compose, mix and automate songs in a single interface. It supports note playback via MIDI or a typing keyboard, and includes a Beat+Bassline Editor and a Piano Roll Editor for working with patterns and notes. It bundles 16 built-in synthesizers, including emulations of the Roland TB-303, Commodore 64 SID, NES, GameBoy and Yamaha OPL2 chips, plus embedded ZynAddSubFx. Sample and instrument formats include SoundFont (SF2), GIG and GUS, and it can host VST instruments and effects and LADSPA effect plugins. Built-in effects include a compressor, limiter, delay, reverb, distortion, bass enhancer, graphic and parametric equalizers, and a spectrum analyzer.
notable: Built-in emulations of classic chips such as TB-303, C64 SID, NES, GameBoy and OPL2
Supports VST, LADSPA and SoundFont plugins and instruments
Imports MIDI files and Hydrogen project files
caveats: VST effect plug-in support is listed for Linux and Windows only
64-bit Windows needs a 32-bit VST bridge for 32-bit VST instruments
